📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NBC will not air a controversial anti-Israel advertisement again after it drew backlash for airing during Wednesday night’s Saturday Night Live Thanksgiving special.

According to recent reports, A person familiar with the situation told The Hollywood Reporter that senior management was unaware of the advertisement until after it aired. NBCUniversal will now evaluate its advertising approval process to ensure appropriate levels of review.

The 30-second advertisement, titled “Every Three Seconds,” shows a young girl saving money for a year by doing yard work, including mowing the lawn, blowing leaves and shoveling snow, until she raises $400 to buy a bicycle. The ad then cuts to a girl in Gaza, standing on crutches and missing a leg amid rubble, as the narrator draws a comparison between the two scenarios and U.S. military aid to Israel. Related Stories Business NBC Uses Thanksgiving TV to Kickstart 2028 LA Olympics Marketing Push TV Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Postponed as Storm Descends on Northeast.

Sources indicate that “Over a year, she saved $400 for a newly introduced bicycle,” the voiceover states. It then cuts to the girl in Gaza. “Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this.”.

It has been revealed that the advertisement was paid for by the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project, or IMEU Policy Project. This pro-Palestinian advocacy nonprofit supports ending U.S. military aid to Israel. The group’s campaign, titled “No More for Israel,” encourages viewers to contact their congressional representatives to oppose continued military assistance to the country.

After the advertisement aired, several Jewish and pro-Israel organizations criticized NBC for broadcasting the spot.

Anti-Defamation League CEO Jonathan Greenblatt criticized the network in a post on X, writing, “Again and again, why do people in positions of authority fail to demonstrate basic decency, let alone respect, for the Jewish community? At a moment of escalating antisemitism, there is no rationale to justify fanning the flames with such a twisted narrative.”.

B’nai B’rith International also condemned the advertisement in a Facebook post.

“Shame on NBC,” the nonprofit wrote. “The suffering of innocent civilians is a tragedy. But using a child’s pain to spread a twisted, one-sided story that blames the Jewish state, and by extension Jews everywhere, is disgusting.”.

Jim Berk, CEO of the Simon Wiesenthal Center, also shared a statement with THR criticizing the network for airing the advertisement.

“The advertisement’s imagery, an American child’s hardship set against the anguish of a child in Gaza, offers viewers a seductive but unsubstantiated narrative: that the struggles of American families are somehow bound up with U.S. support for Israel,” the statement reads in part. “In collapsing a complex foreign policy into a single, emotionally charged imagery, erases the deeper realities, including the imperative to protect Israeli lives and the very existence of the country itself. By manipulating emotion and stripping it of context, this ad seeks to become a catalyst for hostility.”.

#163427. Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation

Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1243 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronomers have identified an extraordinary pair of quasars dating back to just 900 million years after the Significant Bang.
  • An international research team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, offering a rare glimpse into the earliest stages of cosmic history.
  • Recent findings suggest that although astronomers believe paired quasars should be relatively common, finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronomers have identified an extraordinary pair of quasars dating back to just 900 million years after the Significant Bang. Each is powered by an enormous black hole that somehow grew to an astonishing size when the Universe was still in its infancy. Scientists have no definitive explanation for how these two cosmic giants became so massive so swiftly. The remarkable pair has been given the Hawaiian name Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.

An international research team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, offering a rare glimpse into the earliest stages of cosmic history. Officially designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the pair also holds the record for the closest separation between two known quasars from the early period known as cosmic dawn.

Recent findings suggest that although astronomers believe paired quasars should be relatively common, finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult. Discovering two so close together, especially from such an early period in the Universe's history, makes this finding particularly remarkable.

According to recent reports, the discovery was made possible by combining observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Gemini North telescope on Maunakea, a dormant volcano in Hawai'i. The research was led by Silvia Onorato, a postdoctoral research associate at NSF NOIRLab, and is described in a paper published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

In a recent development, gemini North is one of the two telescopes that make up the International Gemini Observatory. Operated by NSF NOIRLab, the observatory is an international partnership led by the U.S. National Science Foundation, with participation from Canada, Chile, Brazil, Argentina, and the Republic of Korea.

How Giant Black Holes Formed in the Early Universe.

Recent findings suggest that during the first billion years after the Big Bang, the Universe underwent a period of extraordinary transformation. Vast concentrations of invisible matter, known as dark matter halos, collapsed under gravity. The earliest galaxies began producing stars, while increasingly massive galaxies developed the first supermassive black holes at their centers.

Recent findings suggest that as galaxies passed near one another, collided, and sometimes merged, enormous quantities of gas and stars became available to feed their central black holes. Some of the material falling toward these black holes released tremendous amounts of energy. This process, known as accretion, could generate radiation so intense that the glowing region surrounding a black hole outshone every star in its host galaxy.

Astronomers call these extraordinarily luminous objects quasars.

Because galaxy encounters and mergers occur frequently throughout the Universe, researchers expect many quasars to exist in pairs separated by distances smaller than the typical diameter of a galaxy. Yet detecting these systems has remained a major challenge.

According to recent reports, one reason is that a supermassive black hole spends only a relatively brief period in its bright "quasar phase." Another is the enormous distance separating ancient quasars from Earth, which makes them appear extremely faint to ground-based telescopes. Even when both objects are visible, their close proximity can make it difficult to distinguish one from the other.

Two Monster Black Holes That Grew Too Big, Too Fast.

Industry observers note that nāpōwawāʻenakaulua stands out because it is only the third known quasar pair from cosmic dawn. More importantly, its two black holes were already so enormous at such an early stage of cosmic history that existing theories cannot definitively explain their growth.

According to recent reports, the black holes are separated by approximately 18,100 light-years, equivalent to about one-fifth the diameter of the Milky Way. One has an estimated mass of 1.5 billion Suns, while the other weighs approximately 400 million solar masses.

Astronomers see the pair as it appeared only 900 million years after the Big Bang, when the Universe was still populated by relatively young stars, galaxies, and black holes. Finding two black holes comparable in mass to many present-day supermassive black holes at this early time raises difficult questions about how rapidly the first enormous cosmic structures could assemble.

"There is no definitive theoretical explanation for how a single one of these giant quasars exists so early in the age of our Universe, much less two," indicates Onorato. "We observed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua at a time when the Universe was only a thirteenth of its age and astonishingly, its supermassive black holes are just as massive as those we see today.".

Sources indicate that the pair's Hawaiian name reflects the extraordinary forces involved. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua translates to "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the Universe.".

The name was developed through the A Hua He Inoa program, a collaboration involving the ʻImiloa Astronomy Center of Hawaiʻi and the University of Hawai'i's Ka Haka ʻUla O Keʻelikōlani (Hawaiian Language College).[1].

How James Webb and Gemini North Revealed the Hidden Pair.

In a recent development, the discovery began with data collected by the Aether survey, a JWST research program designed to identify and characterize objects from the early Universe. The project is led by Emanuele Paolo Farina, an Associate Scientist at NSF NOIRLab/Gemini.

Industry observers note that using JWST's Near-Infrared Spectrograph Integral Field Unit, the survey assembled observations of 200 quasars. That sample represents approximately 43% of all quasars known from this period of cosmic history.

While visually examining the survey data, researchers noticed something unexpected. A previously identified quasar, J1602+4228A, appeared to have a companion.

Sources indicate that to investigate, the team turned to Gemini North's Gemini Near-Infrared Spectrograph (GNIRS). These observations allowed astronomers to distinguish the two quasars individually, providing crucial evidence about the nature of the system.

In a recent development, obtaining those measurements was an exceptional achievement. The objects are separated by such a small apparent distance, and the companion J1602+4228B is so faint, that resolving them with a telescope on Earth was expected to be nearly impossible.

In a recent development, fortunately, the researchers benefited from exceptionally favorable observing conditions on Maunakea. Clear skies and unusually sharp atmospheric conditions enabled them to gather the necessary observations in just two nights.

"The sky over Maunakea was so clean and sharp that we managed to collect the data in only two nights," notes Onorato.

The team also used Gemini North's Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS) to gather additional information about the system and refine their understanding of the two quasars.[2].

A Newly introduced Clue to the Universe's First Giant Galaxies.

Exactly how Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua formed remains unknown. However, the researchers believe its extraordinary properties could point to an unusually dense concentration of matter in the early Universe.

In such an environment, frequent interactions between young galaxies may have provided enormous supplies of gas, simultaneously accelerating the birth of stars and fueling rapid growth of the black holes at their centers.

If this interpretation is correct, the quasar pair could help scientists understand how the earliest massive galaxies developed alongside their central supermassive black holes.

Industry observers note that "Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua is a really unique environment," states Onorato. "It's a laboratory for astronomers to study how the very first massive galaxies and their central black holes assembled together through direct galaxy interactions during these early times.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor.
  • The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek.
  • According to recent reports, the meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

On Nov. 27, 1885, an astronomer made the first known photograph of a meteor.

The picture was taken by Austro-Hungarian astronomer Ladislaus Weinek. He captured the trail of the meteor on a photographic plate in the Czech Republic.

According to recent reports, the meteor he captured was part of the Andromedid meteor shower. The Andromedids were associated with Biela's Comet, which broke apart in the 1850s.

According to recent reports, when Weinek observed the meteor shower in 1885, it was in the middle of a meteor storm. This means that there were way more meteors than usual. Skywatchers could see thousands of meteors per hour.

Sources indicate that not many stargazers may be be acquainted with the Andromedid meteor shower. What used to be a spectacular annual meteor shower is now hardly even visible.

But in 1885, the Andromedids were an annual treat for skywatchers hoping for a chance to see the remains of Biela's comet (a comet first spotted in 1772 and then found - for the third time - in 1826 by the German astronomer Wilhelm von Biela, from whom it gets its name).

Camera technology has come a long way since 1885, which is good since it is a bit harder to see the Andromedids these days. Instead of photographic plates or digital cameras, astronomers now have to use special tracking equipment to record images of Andromedid meteors.

In 2011, astronomers announced that the meteor shower seemed to be undergoing a resurgence of activity, with 50 meteors per hour, and upticks were expected in 2018 and 2023.

After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from Newly introduced York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.

Latest Update: Micron Technology: China probes US chip maker for cybersecurity risks as tech tension escalates

📅 03 Apr 2023 | ⏱️ 2 min read (485 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNN

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • China has launched a cybersecurity probe into Micron Technology, one of America’s largest memory chip makers, in apparent retaliation after US allies in Asia and Europe announced newly introduced restrictions on the sale of key technology to Beijing.
  • The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) will review products sold by Micron in the country, according to a statement by the watchdog late on Friday.
  • The move is aimed at “ensuring the security of key information infrastructure supply chains, preventing cybersecurity risks caused by hidden product problems, and maintaining national security,” it noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

China has launched a cybersecurity probe into Micron Technology, one of America’s largest memory chip makers, in apparent retaliation after US allies in Asia and Europe announced newly introduced restrictions on the sale of key technology to Beijing.

The Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC) will review products sold by Micron in the country, according to a statement by the watchdog late on Friday.

The move is aimed at “ensuring the security of key information infrastructure supply chains, preventing cybersecurity risks caused by hidden product problems, and maintaining national security,” it noted.

It came on the same day that Japan, a US ally, said it would restrict the export of advanced chip manufacturing equipment to countries including China, following similar moves by the United States and the Netherlands.

Washington and its allies have unveiled curbs on China’s semiconductor industry, which strike at the heart of Beijing’s bid to become a tech superpower.

Last month, the Netherlands also unveiled upcoming restrictions on overseas sales of semiconductor technology, citing the need to protect national security. In October, the United States banned Chinese companies from buying advanced chips and chipmaking equipment without a license.

Micron told CNN it was aware of the review.

It has been revealed that “We are in communication with the CAC and are cooperating fully,” it noted, adding that it stands by the security of its products. “Micron’s product shipments, engineering, manufacturing, sales and other functions are operating as normal.”.

In a recent development, shares in Micron sank 4.4% on Wall Street Friday following the news, the biggest drop in more than three months. On Monday, they closed another 1.2% lower. Micron derives more than 10% of its revenue from China.

In an earlier filing, the Idaho-based firm had warned of such risks.

“The Chinese government may restrict us from participating in the China market or may prevent us from competing effectively with Chinese companies,” it stated last week.

Japan joins the US and Europe in chipmaking curbs on China.

China has strongly criticized restrictions on tech exports, saying last month it “firmly opposes” such measures.

In efforts to boost growth and job creation, Beijing is seeking to woo foreign investments as it grapples with mounting economic challenges. The newly minted premier Li Qiang and several top economic officials have been rolling out the welcome wagon for global CEOs and promising they would “provide a good environment and services.”.

But Beijing has also exerted growing pressure on foreign companies to bring them into line with its agenda.

Last month, authorities closed the Beijing office of Mintz Group, a US corporate intelligence firm, and detained five local staff.

Days earlier, they suspended Deloitte’s operations in Beijing for three months and imposed a fine of $31 million over alleged lapses in its work auditing a state-owned distressed debt manager.

CNN’s Michelle Toh, Junko Ogura, Sandi Sidhu and Chris Lau contributed to the article.

Gayle King‘s son-in-law Virgil Miller has died following a battle with cancer at 45, and the CBS Mornings host will miss next week’s highlights “to help with family matters,” according to People.

A memo sent to staff from executive producer Jon Tower and obtained by People announced Miller’s death. “Mornings Family — I’m sorry to be delivering this sad news,” the message began, as he wrote that “over the Thanksgiving holiday,” Virgil died after a “courageous battle with cancer.”.

“Our thoughts right now are with her daughter, and their two beautiful children. We’re respecting the family and giving them privacy as they get through this difficult time,” the EP added. He also communicated that King is taking a week off “to help with family matters.” Tower further wrote that the host will return to CBS Mornings the week of Dec. 7 after “private arrangements” are made. The Emmy winner commended their nuptials on CBS Mornings in February 2021, and also in a heartfelt Instagram post.

Sources indicate that miller attended Florida A&M University, graduating with a bachelor’s degree in biology in 2003 and a master’s degree in public health in 2005. There, he was a drum major as part of FAMU’s Marching 100.

He went on to serve nearly 13 years in the U.S. House of Representatives, and joined Akin in 2019 as a senior policy and strategy advisor before becoming a senior advisor.

SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for Season 2 of “The Hunting Wives,” now streaming on Netflix.

Earlier this month, Texas shocked the nation by electing Democrats to the governorship, the U.S. Senate and several more key positions during this year’s midterm elections. But the Lone Star State’s politics have always been seen as dynamic and complicated to those in the know — like fans of “The Hunting Wives,” Netflix’s juicy, campy drama series about a group of wealthy, gun-loving and sexually fluid women from East Texas.

It has been revealed that “I love our show, because you see both sides of this coin, and we’re making fun of each side,” notes “The Hunting Wives” star Brittany Snow about the series’ depiction of Texas politics. Co-star Malin Åkerman adds, “We’re not going to say that we had anything to do with it, but there’s all these different people saying, ‘The Hunting Wives’ had something to do with Texas going blue!’ It’s a fun little moment for us right now.”.

Sources indicate that åkerman plays Margo Banks, the housewives’ confident ringleader whose Republican husband Jed (Dermot Mulroney) is a favorite to become governor. But, in Season 1, her beautiful house of cards is torn apart with the arrival of Sophie (Snow), an East Coast liberal who is shocked by the dirty underbelly of her new Southern home. Margo is full of secrets that she’s intent on keeping from Sophie, and thinks she’s in the clear when the two begin falling in love (and deep, deep lust). But Season 1 ended with Sophie discovering that Margo had gotten pregnant by a teenager, Brad (George Ferrier), before having an abortion and murdering Brad’s girlfriend, Abby Jackson (Madison Wolfe), for uncovering the truth. The only saving grace for Margo is that Sophie can’t do anything with the information, because when her brother, Kyle (Michael Aaron Milligan), attempts to intimidate Sophie on Margo’s behalf, Sophie hits him with her car and kills him instantly. Now, they’re both in trouble.

Sources indicate that because Sophie hid Kyle’s body and told no one what she did, Season 2 begins with Margo trying to get back into her good graces. Unaware that Kyle is even dead, she keeps calling his number, getting no response until a panicked Sophie uses AI to deepfake Kyle’s voice and keep the illusion up. In person, Sophie tries her best to avoid Margo, but she can’t control herself. So she uses Kyle’s voice to ask Margo whether any of their relationship was genuine. When Margo answers that it was “100% real,” not just a ploy to cover-up the murder, Sophie is finally ready to get back together. She meets Margo at the Banks’ lake house, where they have sex — which is rudely interrupted by Zelda (Dale Dickey), a woman from Margo’s past, who sneaks up and holds a gun point-blank to Margo’s head.

It has been revealed that zelda is the leader of a biker gang in Alba, Margo’s hometown. She suspects Kyle of impregnating and murdering her underage granddaughter, Ellie (Chloe Guidry), and is attacking Margo to get information about Kyle’s whereabouts. Zelda and the gang don’t believe Margo when she states she has no idea where he is until Sophie blurts out that Kyle couldn’t have killed Ellie because she killed him. Zelda pieces together that it was someone in the gang (Cam Gigandet as Gentle John) and shoots him in the head. Soon, the police show up and the gang gets shot to death. Margo and Sophie are escorted home before they can discuss what happened, and Sophie panics, worrying that Margo will tell the police what happened to Kyle. But she doesn’t. After ignoring several calls from Sophie, Margo highlights up at Sophie’s apartment and forgives her — they’re even, since Margo is a murderer too. The two begin secretly dating again, but Jed and his staff keep Margo on a tight leash during his campaign for governor. So Sophie hatches up a plan: If Margo publicly admits that she’s had an abortion, she’ll be able to tank Jed’s campaign and leave him for Sophie while drumming up enough support and attention to maintain her wealthy lifestyle. But right before the couple is set to make a TV appearance, Jed tells Margo that he knows she killed Abby and that Sophie killed Kyle, and that she needs to be a “dutiful wife” if she wants to keep herself and her girlfriend out of prison. Margo does still confess to cheating on Jed and having an abortion on live TV, but instead of advocating for women’s rights, she calls herself a murderer and says that prayer has allowed her to find redemption. The move is received positively by Jed’s rightwing base, and Sophie freaks out. That night, she confronts Margo, who explains to Sophie that she did it to protect her and that they can never speak again. Sophie is enraged, and says that she’ll release her recording of Margo confessing to Abby’s murder unless Margo gives her $10 million. In a brief epilogue set two years later, Sophie is uber-rich but estranged from Margo. She receives a phone call from a mysterious number and only hears panicked breathing on the other end; it’s Margo, who is covered in blood.

Snow and Åkerman, in one interview, and series creator Rebecca Cutter, in a separate conversation, spoke to Variety about the absolute insanity playing out in their East Texan world.

It has been revealed that brittany Snow: When I read the first episode and realized that one of the first scenes is her having a panic attack in her car, and then she later starts hearing sounds on the phone that are not there — I realized she’s sort of losing her mind, and that embeds in her reasoning through the entire show. She’s losing her mind because she’s losing the piece that she’s addicted to, which is Margo. So he’s just trying to fix the negativity and the guilt and shame she feels. So she’s trying to save her marriage. Maybe that’ll fix it. Or maybe she’ll run away from Margot, and maybe that’ll fix it. Or maybe she’s gonna move into this tiny house. Nothing seems to be fixing this hole, so she’s in a very psychologically dark place at the beginning of this show.

Sources indicate that malin Åkerman: I don’t like when Margo’s not on top — but it is fun to play. Margo is in the doghouse. She’s not in the main mansion. She has these bikers from her past who are chasing after her brother. Everything that could go wrong is going wrong. She doesn’t have Sophie available at all. She’s not answering any of her calls, so we find her in a really tough position, and we just want her to get her power back and get back to the unapologetic, outrageous Margo.

Snow: The car scene in the rain was a really difficult scene because there had to be so many things at once happening. The push-pull of a toxic relationship: “Please stay in my car. I love you. I also need you to get out. Also, I killed your brother. Also, I’m gonna have a nervous breakdown.” And it’s all those levels while looking really, really terrible on my part. Like a drowned rat.

Åkerman: I loved that that was the first scene where we see them together, because there was so much going on and there are high stakes. Hopefully people feel the same way, like, “Oh my god! Just stay! Kiss! Get together!”.

In a recent development, snow: It was a good scene. That kinetic energy that we have. The anger that I have. You trying to win me over. It’s a lot!

It has been revealed that åkerman: I mean, Margo comes first. She’s always gonna have her own back. But I truly think that somewhere deep inside, this is the closest to a feeling of love that Margo has had for anyone. There’s something about Sophie that really draws her in, and she feels the most herself that she’s ever felt. There’s some version of true love, as well as her survival. She can’t turn that off yet because it’s not safe yet to turn it off, and she has to make sure that she’s not going to get called out. So there’s a massive duality there.

Recent findings suggest that rebecca Cutter: It was reverse engineering to get Sophie and Margo back together. The biker gang is looking for Kyle, and [since he isn’t available], who can Margo go to when she’s threatened? Sophie’s the only one that knows she killed Abby. Sophie’s the only one that knows the real her. So having that threat come into her life, in the form of Zelda and the gang, sends her directly to Sophie. Then Sophie, having to interact with Margo through the AI deepfake, falls in love with her all over again and feels guilty about what she’s done. It was this perfect storm bringing them back together. The other thing of that makes their reunion possible is that Sophie has grown and changed a lot over the two seasons. She goes from being a very weak character who feels powerless in her life to being this really formidable woman who is an equal to Margo. And realizing that they’re both killers and they both have that same drive and instinct makes them fall in love all the more.

According to recent reports, snow: That scene is nuts. That was a nuts shoot. We also didn’t know that the song that was going to be behind it all was going to be, like — [she sings an twangy, upbeat melody] — so we’re acting our asses off, screaming and crying, and then when you see the scene, you’re like, “Wow, it’s kind of funny, actually! Comical!”.

According to recent reports, åkerman: You just never know how it’s gonna be edited together. But shooting it was it was a lot, over the course of two or three days. A lot of emotion. Luckily, we shot the two things separately, the intimate scene when Dale Dickey’s character comes in and discovers us, and the living room scene where the shootout happens. It was probably good for us — one mindset to the other. It’s one of my favorite things that Dale Dickey gets to say, with the gun to my head. [While Margo’s head is in between Sophie’s legs, Zelda appears with a gun and says, “Well, lookee lookee what we got here.”].

Snow: The juxtaposition of the show is really encapsulated in that scene. The comedy, the drama, the thriller.

It has been revealed that snow: I hate that scene. Because you really see how desperate Sophie is in that moment. I don’t know if any more veins in my neck and forehead could have popped out. She’s desperate, and she doesn’t know if Margo’s going to forgive her, so the fact that she does is pretty crazy.

Sources indicate that åkerman: I loved that scene. You’re brilliant in it. All the veins. I love it all. I love it all.

Åkerman: It’s a lot, and but I do think that Sophie is the closest thing to family that she has after her brother. We also know that Kyle is very unhinged and unmanageable, and who knows what he may have done to Sophie if she hadn’t have run him over? She didn’t plan on it. There were a lot of factors that she had to think about. She herself is also a murderer, so she kind of understands.

Snow: We have this in common now.

Åkerman: I do think it was a lot to process. But she almost wins that cat-and-mouse chase, because she goes, “Well, now I’m back on top. I get to pull the strings and call the shots.” There are a lot of different elements to why she makes the decision to come in and say, “All right, this is how it’s gonna go. Now I’ve got you under my thumb again.”.

Cutter: Margo is, above all else, a survivor and a schemer. In a very practical sense, she recognizes that Sophie has something on her, with Abby Jackson, and she has something on Sophie, with Kyle. It’s like Russia and the United States. It’s a cold war. But now we’re even, so it’s a great place for them to be.

Snow: Murder brought us together!

Snow: Sophie’s coming from such a nervous breakdown that any forgiveness feels like such an oasis in her mind, and especially because it comes from Margo. There’s hope in that scene. When you see Kyle’s dead body [get discovered], you realize hope is never going to last long on “Hunting Wives.” But that scene puts us on the same playing field, and alludes to the idea that things are going to be OK in their weird world.

Industry observers note that åkerman: I don’t know if I’d say the purest. Afterwards, I think it gets purer. But in that moment, Margo holds onto a few other things other than loving intentions. There’s the power dynamic where she’s also deciding that this is OK, and she is now in charge. You’re not gonna call me out for killing Abby Jackson.

Sources indicate that snow: Our physicality in that scene is interesting, because you’re sitting there the whole time just watching me, and I’m pacing around, doing a tap dance. You’re just like, “Dance, monkey.”.

Åkerman: But afterwards, I loved that part of filming. We love being in love. That is the closest we get to seeing what a real relationship could be like for these two. We go, “Oh my God, they might make it! They might run off into the sunset together, and everyone else gets killed off.” That’s not what happens. But we get to see a little more vulnerability from Margo, and I thought that was a lovely part of Season 2.

Recent findings suggest that cutter: It was crucial to show that the relationship is more than just sex, and that there is this deeper commitment that they’re making to each other to move past this, even though it’s kind of a fucked up commitment. I remember talking in the writers’ room about how Mandy became Margo not by dwelling on the past, but by always being willing to move on, shed her skin and transform. “We’re just gonna take this drink and act like nothing ever happened.” That’s so Margo. That’s what she has to do. She cannot dwell in any past trauma.

Snow: I think she can compartmentalize in a way that’s scary, especially when it comes to her son and her family and what she wants. She sees Margot as a beacon of who she wants to be and who she wants to be with. But she still has to be a good mother, and needs to divorce Graham. So she’s wrestling with the decision to, maybe for the first time in her life, choose herself. And that feels really good to her. She’s going to take a bubble bath in the middle of the day and show up for her girlfriend and do all these things. And then it comes crashing down.

Åkerman: Yeah, I think she had a hopeful moment where she thought maybe this could be their happy ending. There was a glimmer of hope, because that’s the thing that initially attracted her to Sophie. She’s bright and smart, and Margo noticed that about her in that very first scene when we see them together at the NRA party.

Åkerman: I may not have a great answer for you. I think it’s more about the suspense, because we want to believe she’s about to say this, and to give it that really great twist at the end. Sources indicate that snow: But don’t you think she’s taking her power back? Like, “You can’t cage me, Jed. I’m still gonna say what I want.”.

According to recent reports, åkerman: I guess you’re right. Thank you for that!

According to recent reports, cutter: It’s partly to mislead the audience, also because Sophie stated something to her on the phone call earlier: “You could be a hero to half the country.” Margo is a very shrewd politician and understands that if she comes forward and gets ahead of it and frames it a certain way, it could actually add to her own power. She plays a card that could have backfired, but we see that it works — and I will be shocked if, someday, a Republican politician doesn’t play this card. Mark my words.

Sources indicate that snow: Trying to cover up another murder, which always brings them together. I mean, we leave off this season with a cliffhanger, where it’s open to the audience whether Sophie feels like she might hear Margo’s voice or maybe she doesn’t. And Margo’s covered in blood, so we get to see these women in totally different places, physically and mentally, and they’re on a level that makes them feel like equal adversaries in a lot of ways. I just hope for Sophie, in Season 3, to take a chill pill. Maybe some Xanax! To sit in her power and not be so anxious all day. I feel like it’s coming.

Snow: I think she’s going to own herself.

Åkerman: We’re gonna have to watch.

Snow: We’re gonna watch, and we’re gonna like it!

Cutter: I don’t watch that much reality TV, but I think I would have to try it. Imitation is the sincerest form of flattery.

  • The species, known as Aptostichus stephencolberti, is a trapdoor spider that lives in California's coastal dunes.
  • In a recent development, many spiders reach their largest size in the fall after spending the summer feeding, making them familiar symbols of Halloween.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A tiny California spider named after comedian Stephen Colbert is making a big impression on scientists. Although it is only about the size of a quarter, the spider has a genome roughly 50% larger than the human genome.

The species, known as Aptostichus stephencolberti, is a trapdoor spider that lives in California's coastal dunes. Its unusually large genome seems particularly fitting given Colbert's famously pompous television persona on the former Comedy Central show "The Colbert Report.".

In a recent development, many spiders reach their largest size in the fall after spending the summer feeding, making them familiar symbols of Halloween. But this particular spider stands out for something that cannot be seen with the naked eye: the extraordinary amount of DNA packed into its tiny body.

"At 4.6 gigabases, or 4.6 billion DNA base pairs, it's not the largest genome among the spiders, but it's significant," said corresponding author Jason Bond, a professor in the UC Davis Department of Entomology and Nematology.

It has been revealed that according to Bond, this is the first time scientists have sequenced the genome of a spider belonging to this family. The findings were published in the Journal of Heredity.

A Secretive Spider That Hunts From Underground.

Visitors to the coastal dunes of Northern California may unknowingly pass close to these spiders without ever spotting one. Most of their lives unfold beneath the sand, where they remain hidden in carefully constructed burrows.

In a recent development, female trapdoor spiders spend their entire lives underground in tunnels lined with silk. Each burrow has a hinged entrance that blends into its surroundings, allowing the spider to stay concealed while monitoring activity outside.

When an unsuspecting insect or other prey animal approaches, vibrations alert the spider to its presence. At precisely the right moment, the spider bursts through its hidden door to capture its next meal.

According to recent reports, although these spiders are skilled ambush predators, their venom poses no danger to humans. Bond noted that among the more than 50,000 known spider species, only about 30 to 50 have venom known to be toxic to people.

A Spider Genome Bigger Than the Human Genome.

Recent findings suggest that the spider's DNA contains more surprises than its sheer size. Researchers found that its genome includes 52 chromosomes, compared with the 46 chromosomes typically found in human cells, which are organized into 23 pairs.

It has been revealed that however, having a larger genome does not necessarily mean having more genes. In this spider, approximately 77% of the genome consists of repetitive DNA sequences that appear many times throughout its genetic material.

In a recent development, the research also highlights an unusual feature of spider chromosomes. Spiders lack the conventional repetitive DNA sequences associated with telomeres, the protective structures at the ends of chromosomes. This difference could help explain why spider chromosomes appear to evolve more rapidly than those of vertebrates.

"It lends itself to broadening our understanding of spider genome composition and consequently how genomes have evolved across the animal Tree of Life," Bond said.

Why Is the Spider Named After Stephen Colbert?

The story behind the spider's unusual scientific name dates back to 2008, when Stephen Colbert discovered that Bond had named a trapdoor spider after rock musician Neil Young.

Not wanting to be left out, Colbert turned the situation into a comedy segment. During "Who's Not Honoring Me Now?" on "The Colbert Report," he publicly demanded that Bond name a spider in his honor.

Bond agreed, and Aptostichus stephencolberti became Colbert's namesake in the spider world.

Rising Seas Threaten California's Trapdoor Spiders.

Beyond revealing the spider's genetic peculiarities, the research could play an important role in protecting the species.

The genome sequencing effort is part of the California Conservation Genomics project, a state-funded initiative designed to build a collection of genomic information that scientists can use to guide conservation decisions.

Industry observers note that trapdoor spiders generally do not venture far from their burrows, making it difficult for populations to move between habitats. Because their coastal dune environments are already separated into isolated areas, researchers hope genetic information will help them identify distinct populations that may need special protection.

Industry observers note that "We Californians love our beaches and trapdoor spiders share them with us," Bond said. "We're hoping to understand how things like climate change, fire and urbanization might be impacting the genetic diversity of species.".

Aptostichus stephencolberti (the "t" in Colbert is silent) is found only in coastal dunes along a limited stretch of Central California, extending from the San Francisco Bay area to Monterey.

Sources indicate that this restricted range makes the species particularly vulnerable to environmental changes. Rising sea levels could eliminate portions of its coastal habitat, while invasive species pose another significant danger.

"They're going to be incredibly sensitive to sea-level rise, but they're also very sensitive to invasive species," Bond remarked.

Spider Venom Could Hold Clues to Fresh Medicines.

Sources indicate that the potential benefits of studying this spider's genome extend beyond conservation and evolutionary biology. Scientists also hope that understanding spider genetics will help them explore the vast range of chemical compounds found in spider venom.

Some substances identified in spider venoms have shown promise as potential painkillers, while others could be useful in developing new ways to control agricultural pests.

With so many spider species still poorly understood at the genetic level, researchers believe their venoms may contain valuable compounds that have yet to be discovered.

"We don't really know what's out there in terms of untapped natural product diversity for venoms," Bond mentioned.

Sources indicate that the study's additional authors include Stephen Richards, Emma Jochim, Lacie Newton, James Starrett, Ruta Sahasrabudhe and Oanh Nguyen of UC Davis; Eric Beraut, Colin Fairbairn, Samuel Sacco, William Seligmann and Merly Escalona of UC Santa Cruz; Robert D. Cooper of Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University; and H. Bradley Shaffer and Erin Toffelmier of UCLA.

The research received support from the California Conservation Genomics Project, with funding provided to the University of California through the state of California's State Budget Act of 2019, as well as from the National Science Foundation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The biggest shopping event of the year is finally here: Black Friday.

Sources indicate that early Black Friday deals started rolling in weeks ago, but now that the actual holiday is upon us, retailers are in deal overload mode. (That will continue through the weekend into Cyber Monday, and likely a few days beyond.) To avoid getting overwhelmed by the hundreds of thousands of deals, it's good to head into the mega-savings event with a strategy.

From preparing your shopping list to knowing when the major Black Friday sales start and end, we've got you covered on everything you need to know to shop Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

Almost every major retailer started offering Black Friday deals in early to mid-November. That mentioned, some products have gotten additional price cuts on Black Friday proper, which falls on Nov. 27 in 2026.

Amazon: Amazon's Black Friday Week sale runs from Nov. 19 to 30, offering 12 consecutive days of deals.

It has been revealed that best Buy: Black Friday at Best Buy started on Nov. 19 and runs through Nov. 28. Its Cyber Monday sale runs from Nov. 29 to Nov. 30, followed by a Cyber Week sale that extends savings from Dec. 1 to Dec. 6.

Recent findings suggest that the Home Depot: The Home Depot's Black Friday goes from Nov. 26 to Dec. 2. It will host a Cyber Week sale from Dec. 3 to 6.

Kohl's: The department store's Black Friday Week sale has been live since Nov. 22, and it ends Nov. 28.

It has been revealed that lowe's: Lowe's has a relatively short Black Friday sale compared to other retailers. It runs from Nov. 27 to 30.

Target: Target's Black Friday sale kicked off on Nov. 22 and goes through Nov. 29. Its Cyber Monday sale starts on Nov. 30 at 3 a.m. ET.

In a recent development, walmart: Walmart is hosting a Black Friday sale from Nov. 23 to Nov. 29 (with deals online only from Nov. 23 to Nov. 26). Its online-only Cyber Monday sale is scheduled for Nov. 30 to Dec. 2.

Industry observers note that absolutely. Amazon's Black Friday deals cover everything from the year's top tech to home essentials. Each day of the sale features fresh "Today's Big Deals," where select products go on sale for up to 60% off.

On Black Friday and Cyber Monday proper, shoppers get two batches of Substantial Deals: one at 3 a.m. ET and another at 11 a.m. ET. The last time we checked, featured products currently include the Apple Watch SE 3, Bose QuietComfort Headphones, the Theragun Relief, and the last-gen Echo Dot (which comes with a bonus $25 credit for Prime members).

Recent findings suggest that the Apple Store is hosting a Black Friday Savings Event from Nov. 27 to 30, but it's not offering any product discounts during the sale. Instead, it's just giving away free gift cards worth $25 to $300 with the purchase of select devices and accessories. For the best Black Friday Apple deals that actually save you cash, we recommend shopping at third-party retailers like Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Target instead.

Recent findings suggest that target has great Black Friday deals if you're looking for toys, Lego sets, Christmas decor, books, or small kitchen appliances. Target's Deal of the Day offers extra savings on hot items, and you can preview upcoming deals several days before they happen. Its Deals of the Day for actual Black Friday take 50% off pajamas and Crocs. Over the weekend, select skincare items, Disney toys, outdoor decor, and shoes will go on sale at deep discounts.

Walmart doesn't skimp on Black Friday deals, and they tend to compete with the best Amazon sales, like $149 Apple AirPods Pro 3. You can also get the Nespresso Vertuo Pop coffee and espresso maker for a rock-bottom price of $59.

It has been revealed that it's worth paying close attention to Best Buy's doorbuster deals, in particular. They offer ridiculous savings but tend to sell out quickly (RIP, $149.99 Ninja Slushi). Below is a roundup of the top news stories from Germany from Thursday, November 26, 2026:.

Michael Noetzel, the latest justice minister in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, has come under fire for a now-deleted social media post promoting the far-left antifa.

The controversy centers on a photo of Noetzel wearing a T-shirt with the historic 1932 antifa logo and raising his left fist.

Noetzel, a representative of the socialist Left Party, also wrote that it is notable for young people to attend antifa meetings.

Philipp Amthor, who serves as acting head of the state chapter of the conservative CDU, demanded that Noetzel "make an unambiguous statement now regarding his position on left-wing extremist and violence-prone groups within the antifa scene.".

Enrico Schult, who is a parliamentary group leader of the far-right populist AfD, stated: "If you have such a hard time distancing yourself from violent structures, then you are unfit to serve as minister of justice.".

The ministry stated that Noetzel "naturally takes a clear stand against extremism.".

The ministry also identified right-wing extremism as the greatest threat to democracy and that combating it is a priority.

The German government prepares to acquire a stake in the Canada-based artificial intelligence technology firm Cohere for the symbolic sum of €1.

The Digital Ministry confirmed media reports that the Finance Ministry had approved the government's small stake in the multinational manufacturer.

According to a ministry spokesperson, the government is at the moment considering investing a larger sum.

Cohere would commit itself "to helping increase competitiveness in AI in Germany and to securing jobs, research and development and investment in Germany," the spokesperson noted.

He added that the German government would receive "specific governance guarantees that safeguard the goal of digital sovereignty.".

Cohere's goal is to develop sovereign AI services for the public administration, as well as finance, defense, energy, telecommunications, and healthcare.

This technology is designed to operate independently of major US data center operators.

The start of the proceedings was delayed in the morning after the accused developed health problems that required treatment by emergency medical workers, a spokeswoman for a Berlin court said.

Later, however, she was brought into the courtroom in a wheelchair, wearing dark sunglasses.

Industry observers note that several times throughout the afternoon, the defense attorneys noted their client was feeling nauseous, and a bucket was brought in. A doctor was present in the courtroom.

The trial is expected to last until May 2027.

Read more about the charges against the woman, as well as the diplomatic fallout caused by the case.

IG Metall, representing millions of workers in Germany's metal and electrical industry, is the country's largest trade union.

The deal came after more than 24 hours of talks with employers.

Read the full story on what the union and industry leaders agreed to.

Germany national player Laura Freigang has been banned from playing until October 7, 2027, over three doping tests she missed, meaning that she will not be available to participate in the World Cup in Brazil next year, the German Football Federation (DFB) said in a statement on Thursday.

The ban comes amid a settlement between Freigang, 28, who is also the captain of Frankfurt Eintracht, and the DFB, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) and Germany's National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA).

Freigang has been the subject of proceedings for several months, having been accused of not being at the location she specified for a doping control on three occasions between March 2025 and February 2026.

In June, she stated that the missed tests "were not deliberately avoided appointments but inconsistencies or misunderstandings in the comprehensive details that have to be updated daily and which we as national team players have to update in the system on a daily and hourly basis.".

Freigang has played 45 times for Germany, scoring 17 goals.

However, she has not recently been a regular in the team.

Read the full story on why Freigang will miss the 2027 World Cup.

The archdiocese in the western city of Cologne was ordered on Wednesday to pay a woman who was sexually abused by a priest for years €550,000 ($601,865) in damages — the highest amount a German court has ever awarded to a victim of abuse in theCatholic Church.

That amount will, however, by offset by the €360,000 that the Catholic Church's Independent Commission for Recognition Payments has already paid to the claimant.

The woman had previously had her claim rejected by the Cologne Regional Court, which, although it accepted that the victim had been severely sexually abused by a priest in the 1970s and 1980s, argued that the archdiocese could not be made responsible for the crimes because the man had acted "more or less as a private individual.".

The higher regional court has now overturned that ruling at an appeal, saying that the priest had approached the claimant "under the cover of his church work" when he was a deacon.

It said he used his standing in the church to be allowed to take in foster children, of whom the claimant was one.

The priest was sentenced to 12 years in prison in 2022.

German Foreign MinisterJohann Wadephul has warned against an expansion of the Ukraine conflict into other regions after the Ukrainian attacks on Russian ships in Libya.

"Ukraine's ​right to self-defense is undisputed and we ​do support Ukraine, but I strongly ⁠warn ​against allowing ​this conflict to spread ​geographically," he ‌noted at ​a ⁠press conference in Berlin with ⁠his ​Romanian counterpart Dan Neculaescu.

Wadephul also condemned reported Russian attacks on two foreign freight ships mentioned to be carrying grain near Ukraine's Black Sea port of Odesa, saying such attacks did not concern only the security of nearby nations but also the food security of people in the Global South.

"It is clear that we cannot accept drone attacks on trading vessels," he said. "NATO will therefore step up its engagement in the region.".

German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has called for closer economic and political partnerships with African countries as he wound up what was probably his last trip to the continent as head of state.

Speaking in Kenya, Steinmeier noted that there were great variations in the state of development between individual countries and even within some of them.

"But I believe it is worthwhile investing in Africa and in relations with African countries," he noted.

According to recent reports, he stated this was not just meant with a view to possible investment by German companies drawn by Africa's mostly young national populations and developing markets. "That is true, but we should not limit our view to that. Many African countries now have political weight and growing self-confidence and want a say in shaping the future of the world," he said. "Africa, it has become clear, is a continent that requires patience if you want to discover it," Steinmeier said. "There is no single Africa, but very many.".

Before Kenya, Steinmeier visited Ivory Coast and Ghana. On the final day of his trip, he went to the Crescent Island nature reserve on Lake Naivasha, an area under threat from climate change.

Chocolate manufacturers in Germany produced less in 2025 than the year before.

According to figures from the Federal Statistical Office (Destatis) released on Thursday, around 1 million metric tons (1.1 US tons) of chocolate products containing cocoa were made in Germany in 2025, compared with 1.1 million tons in 2024.

This represents a reduction of 5.7%.

Much of the chocolate produced in Germany is exported (916,200 tons in 2025), while considerable amounts are also imported (530,000 tons in 2025), with a quarter of that amount coming from neighboring Belgium.

Altogether 13.4% of exports went to France, followed by Poland (9.6%) and the UK (9.3%).

According to Destatis, citing the EU's statistical agency Eurostat, Germany remains the European leader in the production of gingerbread, or Lebkuchen, manufacturing 39.4% of the entire EU supply of the sweet treat, compared with Poland on 17.3% and the Netherlands on 17%.

German authorities say that two Iraqi citizens believed to be members of a pro-Iranian terrorist group have been arrested on suspicion of having planned a number of anti-Jewish attacks, including on a synagogue in the western city of Cologne.

You can read more about the arrests and the charges laid against the two men in our article: Germany: 2 arrested, suspected of plotting synagogue attack.

A survey by police union GdP has shown that some 69% of police in Germany are in favor of a ban on private fireworks on New Year's Eve.

According to the survey of 9,000 members, more than 70% feel that the situation for police on the evening would improve if such a ban were in place.

Altogether 54% of respondents who had been on duty during the past 10 years of New Year's Eve festivities reported having been in a dangerous or threatening situation caused by fireworks.

A whole 195 respondents stated they had been injured by fireworks on the evening.

Recent findings suggest that the poll was prompted by an open letter to Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt by a group calling itself #böllerciao (Goodbye firecrackers) with some 1.17 million signatories. The name is a play on the famous anti-Nazi song Bella Ciao.

The group includes 86 organizations, among them Environmental Action Germany (DUH) and the GdP, who have called for a ban on private fireworks to protect people, emergency personnel, animals and the environment.

Aims foreseeing a rise of €1 billion ($1.1 billion) in the budget for the Interior Ministry have been approved by the three parties in Germany's coalition government, after much debate centering on something that makes up a relatively small proportion of that money: the controversial planned centers for rejected asylum seekers in Rwanda.

According to Klaus-Peter Willsch of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU), just €5 million are earmarked for the so-called return hubs, shared between several European countries.

He noted the €20 million that has often been cited as being for the Rwanda migration centers was not only for the hubs in that country, but for other potential projects in third countries as well.

Despite the relatively small amounts of money involved, the Rwanda plans devised by Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt of the Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU) along with Austria, Denmark, the Netherlands and Greece came under fire not only from coalition partners the Social Democrats (SPD) but particularly from opposition parties.

The Green Party and the Left Party both rejected the idea for ethical reasons, with Green lawmaker Leon Eckert speaking of "state-organized human trafficking," while Dietmar Bartsch of the Left pointed out that the deal was being made with an authoritarian regime.

The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD), for its part, stated it found the looks too soft, with parliamentarian Marcus Bühl calling them a "smoke screen," as just 20 rejected asylum-seekers from Germany were to be initially sent to Rwanda under the scheme.

In a recent development, dobrindt defended the scheme, saying that the opposition was trying to stir up controversy about a concept that had been approved at European level. He also called criticism of the political system in Rwanda inappropriate, citing a school for Afghan girls that had been set up in the country amid the ban on secondary education for females by the Taliban government.

The interior minister also praised the additional funds given to his ministry as a contribution to Germany's defense against hybrid attacks from Russia, with a rise in the budgets of both the IT security and the civic protection departments.

The draft 2027 budget, which was approved by the conservative CDU/CSU bloc and the SPD, however includes less funding for the BAMF migration authority (from €999 million in 2026 to €994 million) and for integration aid for migrants and refugees (down €328 million to €1.07 billion).

The trial of a German-Ukrainian woman due to go on trial on Thursday on charges of spying for Russia was delayed in the morning after the accused developed health problems that required treatment by emergency medical workers, a spokeswoman for a Berlin court mentioned.

It was not clear whether her trial could go ahead as planned.

The 57-year-old woman has been accused of passing information to an officer from Russia's GRU intelligence agency who was posing as a diplomat at the Russian Embassy in Berlin.

Prosecutors allege that she used contacts with  current and former German Defense Ministry officials to collect information on military aid for Ukraine, drone test sites and the arms industry.

She also faces accusation of having provided her alleged handler access to key political events in Berlin.

The woman was arrested in late January, with the alleged involvement of the Russian Embassy causing considerable outrage in Berlin.

Russia's ambassador was summoned over the incident, and the handler — identified by news weekly Der Spiegel as the embassy's deputy military attache — was expelled from Germany.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Bundestag is conducting its concluding debates on the budget for 2027 ahead of a final vote scheduled for Friday.

On Thursday, the focus will initially be on the individual budget for the Interior Ministry led by Alexander Dobrindt of the conservative Bavarian Christian Social Union (CSU), the sister party of Chancellor Friedrich Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU).

The government foresees that the ministry, which is responsible for the federal police and the domestic intelligence agency BfV, among other things, will receive some €16.8 billion in 2027 ($18.43 billion), around €1 billion more than this year.

Lawmakers will then go on to debate the individual budgets for the Economics and Energy Ministry, the Ministry for Housing, Urban Development and Building, the Ministry of Food and Agriculture and the Ministry for Education, Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth.

Opening the debates on Wednesday, Merz described the tight budget as an "accurate reflection" of the "difficult situation as a country — geopolitically, technologically, and demographically" — that Germany finds itself in.

"We will no longer be able to afford everything with tax revenue that we have become all too accustomed to for far too long," Merz added.

Rejecting cheap fabrics, higher prices: Why shoppers are asking for better clothes

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1283 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.
  • Recent findings suggest that the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S.
  • Recent findings suggest that apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Clothing isn't made like it used to be, and more shoppers are taking notice.

Recent findings suggest that the makeup of apparel imported into the U.S. has shifted in recent years. In 2010, about 60% of clothing was predominantly made from cotton. Now, that total is around 45%, while predominantly synthetic fabrics such as polyester and nylon comprise the majority of imports.

Recent findings suggest that apparel prices generally declined over the two decades leading up to the pandemic, according to the consumer price index. Since 2020, they have soared to record highs.

It's starting to change habits for consumers who are paying more for food, gas, rent and other staples. As shoppers shell out more for clothes, they're increasingly making sure the garments are worth the cost.

Consulting firm AlixPartners' 2026 Consumer Sentiment Index, which surveyed more than 9,000 shoppers, found that consumers are scrutinizing labels more closely and rejecting cheap materials sold at a premium.

"If it's not a natural material, a retailer brand who passes it off as it is, they're really becoming very low on consumers' minds," remarked Sonia Lapinsky, head of fashion at AlixPartners.

Recent findings suggest that fast fashion brands like Forever 21 and H&M exploded in popularity during the early 2000s and 2010s, bringing trendy clothing to shelves swiftly at low prices. Then came ultra-fast fashion, with brands like Shein and Fashion Nova pumping out fresh garments at even quicker speeds and lower price points — made possible in part through the use of inexpensive, synthetic fabrics.

"We got to a point where the pendulum just swung too far in that direction. And we've actually begun to see a reversal," remarked U.S. Bancorp BTIG consumer analyst Janine Stichter. "Quality matters a lot more ... over the last three or four years than it has in the previous 10 or 20.".

But quality, which shoppers often tie directly to material, can come at a higher cost.

The average unit price of apparel imported to the U.S. between January and August was $2.64 per square meter for garments that were predominantly synthetic fiber, like polyester and nylon, compared with $3.67 for items that were largely cotton, according to data from the U.S. Commerce Department's Office of Textiles and Apparel.

When comparing those 2026 figures to 2010, synthetic fiber apparel import costs have climbed around 11%, while cotton apparel costs have risen 21%.

"If you're appealing to a more value-sensitive customer, you either reduce the quality, or you negotiate with suppliers to try to share some of the cost or you maybe absorb the cost … and perhaps hope to crank a higher volume of product to make up for it," noted Bernstein Research senior retail analyst Aneesha Sherman.

Though polyester is cheaper, experts point out that's not necessarily a bad thing. It can help clothing hold its shape and wick away sweat.

Recent findings suggest that sherman believes the athleisure boom is a primary factor in the shift toward polyester. She noted that from 2015 to 2025, sports apparel was growing at a 4.9% rate in the U.S., versus 2.6% for all apparel and footwear, according to Euromonitor data.

Recent findings suggest that "There probably is some quality trade down as well happening there," Sherman stated. "But I think both these trends are conflated.".

Nonetheless, backlash to synthetic materials is growing. Gen Z has even repurposed the word "polyester" as an insult to mean generally low-quality or fake.

Concerns have also grown about the environment and human health surrounding petroleum-based clothing, as more research indicates microplastics can leach from polyester clothing when washed.

It's led consumers to reexamine what materials are in their clothing.

Apparel prices have risen coming out of the pandemic, as demand outpaced supply and allowed companies to raise prices, said BTIG's Stichter. Tariffs and the Iran war followed, raising costs for businesses — and prices for consumers.

Petroleum is the basis of many synthetic fibers, and oil prices have skyrocketed since the start of the Iran war.

The same factors that helped drive up prices of clothing — Covid, tariffs and war — also affected clothing quality.

"Companies had to move around their supply chains in the post-Covid period," stated Stichter. "They had to find ways to take costs out, and sometimes that meant using less expensive fabrics.".

Those factors compounded a more-than-decade-long shift away from manufacturing in China.

Sheng Lu, a fashion and apparel studies professor at the University of Delaware, whose research focuses on the economics of the global textile industry, stated China's established history with clothing production means it has higher-skilled workers, state-of-the-art-equipment and better material management compared with emerging manufacturing destinations such as Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Cambodia.

In a recent development, "They mostly serve the value market and the mass market. And I think the reason why they're not ready to make higher-quality luxury and premium products really reflects the kind of skill sets you can expect when you source from these countries," said Lu.

In a recent development, alixPartners' Lapinsky said these countries that manufacture at a lower cost sometimes have to still ship the raw materials from China, which can extend the timeline to make clothing. That means taking earlier bets on trends and then discounting if products don't sell well.

"If you have to mark down that product because the consumer doesn't want it as much, your net margin might actually be worse than if you were to just invest in quality in the first place," said BTIG's Stichter.

And as material costs rise for synthetic fibers, Stichter also said she believes it could further influence companies to use more natural fabrics moving forward.

Companies prioritizing quality are winning in this environment.

Recent findings suggest that ralph Lauren's stock is up around 85% over the past two years. Around 90% of its apparel is primarily made of cotton, leather, wool, viscose, cashmere or silk, according to its 2026 sustainability report. In its fiscal 2026, the organization said it sold more products at full price and reduced markdowns.

Meanwhile, direct-to-consumer clothing brand Quince, which centers its brand identity around natural materials, reached a $10 billion valuation this year.

The brand jumped 16 spots to No. 3 for best resale value in online consignment retailer ThredUp's 2025 report. Organic cotton retailer Pact jumped 20 spots on that list to No. 8, illustrating the potential role materials are playing in brand recognition.

Alternatively, the 2026 AlixPartners report, which ranks sentiment for brands in different retail categories, found shoppers are viewing some fast fashion brands less favorably. Both Shein and Zara dropped three spots — to fifth and seventh place, respectively — in terms of sentiment in the young adult specialty category.

Shein passed higher tariff costs onto shoppers in 2025 and then blamed a sales slowdown on those higher prices. The ultra-fast fashion retailer saw its year-over-year share of U.S. apparel, accessories and footwear card spending decrease in the fourth quarter of 2025 and first two quarters of 2026, according to Consumer Edge.

Shein did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Sources indicate that though Zara fell in AlixPartners' Consumer Sentiment Index, it has continued to grow sales and profits year over year. Even so, Lapinsky stated worsening consumer views are something to watch, even if the company is doing well.

"What we found over the years with this consumer sentiment index is that sometimes it will be a bit of a leading indicator of what's to come," mentioned AlixPartners' Lapinsky. "I'm not saying that this is going to be true for Zara, but I think that's one thing that we'll be watching as we look in the upcoming quarters and into 2027.".

#163417. Latest Update: Astronomers may have discovered a black hole born before the first stars

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (821 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Astronomers may have discovered a black hole born before the first stars

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that on December 18, 2019, astronomers recorded something unusual happening to a star in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.
  • Researchers have named the mysterious object Phoebe, but its true identity remains unknown.
  • Recent findings suggest that astronomers at Swinburne University in Melbourne identified the signal while examining observations from a survey that frequently monitored stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that on December 18, 2019, astronomers recorded something unusual happening to a star in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a satellite galaxy of the Milky Way. For approximately one hour, the star gradually grew brighter before fading back to its usual appearance. The change was smooth and symmetrical, with no sudden explosion or flare. It looked as though an invisible object had moved between Earth and the star, bending its light in our direction. Afterward, the star returned to normal and highlighted no further changes in brightness.

Researchers have named the mysterious object Phoebe, but its true identity remains unknown. The event appears to be an example of gravitational microlensing, a phenomenon predicted by Einstein's general theory of relativity. When a compact object with sufficient mass passes in front of a distant star, its gravity bends the star's light and temporarily magnifies its brightness. This produces a recognizable pattern that differs from the changes caused by variable stars, stellar flares, or passing asteroids.

Recent findings suggest that astronomers at Swinburne University in Melbourne identified the signal while examining observations from a survey that frequently monitored stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud. The distinctive pattern convinced the team that they had detected a genuine gravitational microlensing event. What remained uncertain was the nature of the invisible object responsible.

Three Possible Explanations for the Mysterious Object.

In a recent development, researchers have identified three potential explanations for Phoebe. One possibility is a rogue planet that was expelled from its original solar system and now travels alone through the Milky Way. Another is a similar wandering planet located within the Large Magellanic Cloud. If the second explanation proves correct, Phoebe would become the first planet discovered through gravitational microlensing beyond our galaxy.

Sources indicate that the third possibility is far more extraordinary. Phoebe could be a primordial black hole, an ancient object that formed in the earliest moments of the universe. Unlike ordinary black holes, which develop when massive stars collapse, primordial black holes could have emerged from extremely dense regions of space during the first fractions of a second after the Major Bang. Such objects would have formed long before the first stars appeared.

A One-Hour Signal Reveals a Surprising Clue.

According to recent reports, the unusually short duration of the brightening provides an important clue about Phoebe's mass. Gravitational microlensing events depend partly on how massive the intervening object is. Generally, lighter objects produce shorter events, although their speed and position also influence how long the magnification lasts.

According to recent reports, phoebe's signal lasted approximately 60 minutes, placing it near the detection limit of current astronomical surveys. Using the observed duration and their models of the event, researchers estimated that the object has a mass roughly three times that of the Moon. That would make it considerably less massive than any planet in our solar system and far too small to be a conventional black hole formed by a collapsing star.

Black holes produced through stellar collapse typically have masses of at least about five times that of the Sun. Phoebe's estimated mass falls enormously below that threshold. If the mysterious object really is a black hole, its tiny mass would point toward a primordial origin rather than the death of a star.

Could Phoebe Be a Primordial Black Hole Linked to Dark Matter?

It has been revealed that to investigate where Phoebe might belong, the researchers compared the likelihood that the object originated from different populations. These included stars in the Milky Way, stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud, and objects associated with the surrounding dark matter halo.

The results strongly favored the dark matter halo. According to the team's calculations, Phoebe is approximately 100,000 times more likely to belong to this population than to one associated with ordinary stellar matter. This enormous difference makes a potential connection to dark matter particularly intriguing, although it does not establish that Phoebe is a primordial black hole.

If the primordial black hole interpretation is correct, Phoebe could be among the oldest objects ever detected. It may have formed before the first atoms and stars existed, when the universe was still experiencing the extreme conditions that followed the Substantial Bang.

It has been revealed that for roughly 13 billion years, such an object could have traveled unseen through space, leaving almost no trace of its existence. Then, on a single night in December 2019, its gravity may have briefly magnified the light of a distant star, offering astronomers a remarkable glimpse of something born near the very beginning of the universe.
